## Sentiment

Net sentiment is the article's positive probability minus its negative probability, from
−1 (certainly negative) to +1 (certainly positive).

```{r sentiment-data, include=FALSE}
country_avg <- scores |>
  group_by(country) |>
  summarise(
    positive = mean(bert_positive),
    neutral  = mean(bert_neutral),
    negative = mean(bert_negative),
    net      = mean(bert_net),
    n        = n(),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(label = paste0(country, " (n=", comma(n), ")"))

outlet_avg <- scores |>
  group_by(country, outlet_name, english) |>
  summarise(
    net = mean(bert_net),
    se  = sd(bert_net) / sqrt(n()),
    n   = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

corpus_mean <- mean(scores$bert_net)

# Numbers quoted in the notes
f2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
f2n <- function(x) sub("^-", "−", sprintf("%.2f", x))      # typographic minus
ca <- country_avg |> filter(country %in% big_countries)
de <- filter(country_avg, country == "Germany")
eng <- filter(scores, english)
isr_gap <- t.test(bert_net ~ (country == "Israel"), data = eng)
conf_by <- scores |>
  filter(country %in% big_countries) |>
  mutate(confidence = pmax(bert_positive, bert_neutral, bert_negative)) |>
  group_by(country) |>
  summarise(med = median(confidence), above80 = mean(confidence >= 0.8), .groups = "drop")
oa <- outlet_avg |> filter(n >= MIN_OUTLET_N)
ansa <- filter(oa, outlet_name == "ANSA")$net
corriere <- filter(oa, outlet_name == "Corriere della Sera")$net
```

### Average class probabilities by country

```{r heatmap, fig.height=5, fig.width=8}
country_avg |>
  pivot_longer(c(positive, neutral, negative), names_to = "sentiment", values_to = "prob") |>
  mutate(sentiment = factor(sentiment, levels = c("positive", "neutral", "negative"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sentiment, y = reorder(label, net), fill = prob)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", prob), color = prob > 0.55), size = 3.6,
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "black", "FALSE" = "white")) +
  scale_fill_viridis(option = "plasma", name = "Mean probability", limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Mean sentiment probabilities by country",
       subtitle = "Rows ordered by net sentiment, least negative at the top",
       x = "Sentiment class", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"))
```

The negative class dominates everywhere (mean probability between `r f2(min(ca$negative))`
and `r f2(max(ca$negative))`), and the mean positive probability never exceeds
`r f2(max(ca$positive))`. Germany is the exception: its mean neutral probability is
`r f2(de$neutral)`, against `r f2(mean(scores$bert_neutral))` for the corpus as a whole.

### Net sentiment by outlet

```{r outlet-bars, fig.height=8, fig.width=10}
outlet_avg |>
  filter(n >= MIN_OUTLET_N) |>
  mutate(
    direction = ifelse(net > corpus_mean, "above corpus mean", "below corpus mean"),
    outlet    = reorder(paste0(outlet_name, " (", n, ")"), net)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = net, y = outlet, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = corpus_mean, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~country, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("above corpus mean" = "#2196F3", "below corpus mean" = "#F44336"),
                    name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title = "Net sentiment by outlet",
    subtitle = paste0("Outlets with at least ", MIN_OUTLET_N,
                      " articles (n in brackets); dashed line = corpus mean"),
    x = "Net sentiment", y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

Outlets in the same country can differ as much as countries do. In Italy, ANSA
(`r f2n(ansa)`) and Corriere della Sera (`r f2n(corriere)`) sit near opposite ends of the
full ranking, so a country average partly reflects which outlets happen to be in the sample.

### Distribution of net sentiment

```{r ridges, fig.height=7, fig.width=9, message=FALSE}
scores |>
  filter(country %in% big_countries) |>
  left_join(select(country_avg, country, label), by = "country") |>
  mutate(label = reorder(label, bert_net, FUN = mean)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = bert_net, y = label, fill = after_stat(x))) +
  geom_density_ridges_gradient(scale = 2, rel_min_height = 0.01) +
  scale_fill_viridis(option = "cividis", name = "Net sentiment") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of net sentiment by country",
    subtitle = paste0("Countries with at least ", MIN_COUNTRY_N, " articles"),
    x = "Net sentiment", y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

The distributions overlap almost completely and sit below zero:
`r percent(mean(scores$bert_net < 0), accuracy = 0.1)` of all articles have negative net
sentiment. The gap between the least and most negative countries (`r f2(max(ca$net) - min(ca$net))`)
is smaller than the spread of single articles (standard deviation `r f2(sd(scores$bert_net))`).

### Outlets ranked by net sentiment

```{r outlet-ranking, fig.height=8, fig.width=9}
outlet_avg |>
  filter(n >= MIN_OUTLET_N) |>
  mutate(
    label = reorder(paste0(outlet_name, " (", country, ", ", n, ")"), net),
    group = ifelse(english, "English-language", "Other languages")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = net, y = label, color = group)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = corpus_mean, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = net - 1.96 * se, xmax = net + 1.96 * se), width = 0) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("English-language" = "#1976D2", "Other languages" = "#E65100"),
                     name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title = "Outlets ranked by mean net sentiment",
    subtitle = paste0("Mean with 95% confidence interval; outlets with at least ",
                      MIN_OUTLET_N, " articles; dashed line = corpus mean"),
    x = "Net sentiment", y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

German and Israeli outlets are the least negative; the BBC, the Guardian, Fox News, the Daily
Mail, Al Jazeera and Corriere della Sera the most. With these sample sizes only gaps of about
0.1 or more are clearly distinguishable. Among English-language sources, Israeli outlets are
less negative than the others by `r f2(abs(diff(isr_gap$estimate)))` (95% CI
`r f2(min(abs(isr_gap$conf.int)))` to `r f2(max(abs(isr_gap$conf.int)))`).

### Model confidence

GDELT tone scores are not available through the Doc API, so the model cannot be checked
against them. As a weaker check, the chart shows the model's **confidence**: the probability
it gives to the class it picks. With three classes the minimum is 1/3.

```{r confidence, fig.height=6, fig.width=9, message=FALSE}
scores |>
  filter(country %in% big_countries) |>
  mutate(
    confidence = pmax(bert_positive, bert_neutral, bert_negative),
    country    = reorder(country, confidence, FUN = median)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = confidence, y = country, fill = after_stat(x))) +
  geom_density_ridges_gradient(scale = 1.8, rel_min_height = 0.01,
                               quantile_lines = TRUE, quantiles = 2) +
  scale_fill_viridis(option = "magma", name = "Confidence", direction = -1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(1/3, 1)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.8, linetype = "dashed", color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  labs(
    title = "Model confidence by country",
    subtitle = "Black line = median; dashed line = 0.80",
    x = "Probability of the predicted class", y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

Median confidence runs from `r f2(min(conf_by$med))` to `r f2(max(conf_by$med))`: below 0.80
in every country, and only `r percent(min(conf_by$above80), accuracy = 1)` to
`r percent(max(conf_by$above80), accuracy = 1)` of articles per country pass that mark. The
model often hesitates between *negative* and *neutral* on long news texts, so the class
shares in this report are better read as tendencies than as clean labels.
